title: Tuesday, September 15, 2026

headline.title: The AI-slowdown trade is being un-priced, and the counter-punch came from Jensen Huang. NVIDIA's CEO told President Trump “we're not going to let an AI slowdown happen,” per TechCrunch — a direct answer to the Amodei essay that erased a trillion dollars of semiconductor value on Monday. The tape is reversing accordingly: every name that was destroyed yesterday is green this morning, and every name that was bid is giving it back. LRCX +2.09%, INTC +1.50%, ARM +1.37%, SNDK +1.03%, MU +1.00%, AMD +0.82%, NVDA +0.52%. Against that, the safety bid is unwinding: FTNT −2.90%, ZS −1.95%, CRWD −1.91%, NET −1.83%, PANW −1.82%.
headline.summary: Monday's split was real and it held every hour of the session — that is the thing to carry into today. The buyers finished ABOVE their gaps (GOOGL +3.22%, META +2.71%, MSFT +1.97%), the sellers finished weak (ARM −9.74% closed within a dollar of its low, VRT −7.65%, DELL −5.82%), and the safety bucket doubled its gap: CRWD closed +13.85% against a +6.54% premarket print. But a two-day round trip is not a trend. The real risk today is not the AI debate at all — it is the 10-year at 5.00%, having tagged 5.04% overnight, with a $13B 20-year auction at 12:00 CT and the Fed deciding tomorrow.

overview:
Futures are close to flat and that understates how much is moving underneath. S&P futures −0.18%, Dow −0.38%, Nasdaq −0.16%, Russell −0.23% — but the index calm is two violent rotations cancelling out. The bond story is the one that matters. The 10-year sits at 5.00%, up 4bp, after touching 5.04% overnight; the 2-year is 4.65%, +2bp, and the 30-year is near 5.33%. Monday was the first time the 10-year crossed 5% intraday since 2023. This is now a global bond selloff, not a US one: European 10-year sovereign yields are up 4–6bp, and the trigger is fiscal. Japan is considering lifting its defense-spending target to 3.5% of GDP from 2.0% while approving a temporary food-sales-tax cut — developed economies expanding fiscal support exactly as bond markets demand higher yields. The Bank of England is moving the other way, planning to stop active sales of 20- and 30-year Gilts specifically to slow rising yields. Watch the $13B 20-year auction at 12:00 CT; a tail there matters more to this tape than anything Dreamforce says.

Oil has not let go, and it escalated again overnight. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure continued after Monday's pipeline shutdown, which had already pushed Brent ~3% higher on the session. WTI +1.0% to $102.37, Brent near $106, with The Wall Street Journal reporting oil executives warning about a fuel crisis. Gold is −0.7% to $4,321 and the dollar index +0.2% to 99.61 — a rising dollar and falling gold alongside rising crude is a rates story, not a fear story. Bitcoin is −2.76% to $76,965 ahead of today's Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act, which needs 60 votes; that weakness is spilling into crypto-linked equities after a strong run.

Today's calendar: September Empire State Manufacturing at 7:30 CT, Bessent's annual testimony to House Financial Services at 9:00 CT, the 20-year auction at 12:00 CT, and the FOMC meeting begins with no communication until tomorrow. Futures now price a 92% chance of a 25bp hike to 3.75%–4.00% — the first increase since July 2023 — and the market is leaning toward two hikes by year-end. Dreamforce's main keynote is 12:00 CT — and CRM is already fading, −1.36%, which is the pattern this book flagged yesterday. China's August data was mixed again: retail sales +0.4% against 0.7–0.8% expected, industrial production +5.2% against 4.8%, fixed-asset investment −7.2%. Weak domestic demand, resilient industry.

watchlist.em_label: MARKS VS MONDAY 9/14 CLOSE — THE ROUND TRIP, AND A 5.00% 10-YEAR

setups: Jensen Huang told Trump “we're not going to let an AI slowdown happen.” That is the most direct possible rebuttal to the essay that repriced the complex, and it came from the company with the most to lose. The entire Monday board has inverted: LRCX +2.09%, INTC +1.50%, ARM +1.37%, MU +1.00% against FTNT −2.90%, ZS −1.95%, CRWD −1.91%, PANW −1.82%. The question that decides the week: was Monday a one-day panic that is now fully unwound, or is this the dead-cat bounce inside a repricing that has further to run? Neither side has been settled by a datapoint — both moves came from executives talking. The Fed decides tomorrow, so nobody has to answer today.
The risk nobody is discussing this morning

Everything above is a sector rotation inside a flat index. The thing that can actually move the whole tape is the bond market, and it is at a level that matters: the 10-year printed 5.04% overnight and sits at 5.00%, with the 2-year at 4.65%. European sovereigns are up 4–6bp alongside. The driver is fiscal — Japan weighing a defense-spending increase to 3.5% of GDP from 2.0% while cutting food tax, and the BoE having to halt long-Gilt sales to slow its own yields. The $13B 20-year auction at 12:00 CT is the live test, one day before a Fed decision now priced at 92% for a hike to 3.75–4.00%, the first since July 2023. A weak auction into a 5% 10-year is a bigger problem for equities than the AI debate.

Yesterday this book ranked CRM third and said the setup was a known fade pattern presenting as strength. It closed Monday +4.73% and is now −1.36% premarket, into the 12:00 CT keynote. Our five-event study: Dreamforce ran 1.06x volume / 1.21 ATR in 2025 and 0.91x / 0.76 ATR in 2024, and faded both years. The real event is tomorrow 3:00 CT — the Investor & Analyst Session, which carries a financial framework, landing at the bell on decision day. INTU is doing the same thing, −1.44% after closing +5.47%, two days before its own investor day.

prep.lead: ⚠ No prep sheet in hand yet — this is the tape's read, not Marcus's. Yesterday's sheet scored well: CRWD was called a bullish kicker and closed +13.85%; RBLX's gap fill at 48.57 was taken out and it closed 51.29, +12.73%; AAPL never cleared the 336.22 call entry, closed 333.08, and was correctly a no-trade by its own rule.

darkpool.note: The baton passed from META back to NVDA, and it argues against this morning's bounce being empty. Monday's largest print on the whole board ex-ETF was NVDA $796.4M at the ASK, after hours — landing the same night the slow-the-AI story took the stock down 2–3%. NVDA now tops cumulative flow at $4.4B (ask) ahead of MU $3.6B (mixed) and AVGO $3.3B (bid). The semis that wore Monday's selling are exactly where the after-hours size concentrated — NVDA at the ask, AVGO $779M (bid), LRCX $316M (bid) after its −8.4% session — and that same group is gapping up 1–2% this morning. Ask-side size into a falling name reads like someone stepping in, but a side is a lean and not a verdict. The caution sits in the same name: NVDA's own morning $50M print came at the BID, the opposite side of last night's $796M ask. Size is working both sides into the Fed.
darkpool.right_note: Largest block on the board: LULU $300P 12/18 at $34.4M, a floor put block out to December, biggest single ticket by a wide margin. Largest sweep: NVDA $220P 09/18 at $0.8M — struck ABOVE where NVDA trades premarket and expiring Friday on triple witching, two days after the decision. On the ETF side SPY $1.0B (ask, AH) topped the board, making it six straight sessions an S&P 500 tracker print has been the tape's largest, joined by bond money in BGFI $372M (mixed) the night before the Fed convenes.
